- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly after a spike in the middle of the period.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert toward historical mean but overshoot or undershoot by 2–3% relative to true values.
- Model lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp upward spikes.
- Model fails to capture the “post-spike” correction phase — it overreacts to short-term volatility and doesn’t smoothly transition to mean-reverting levels.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases following a low point in the 30-day history.
- Model overestimates the volatility of the last 5–7 days, leading to overconfident high forecasts.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower prices in the first 10 days of the forecast, then gradually adjusts — suggesting a delayed response to recent price trends.
